  "markdown_report": "At 0% progress, prioritize a small SASRec extension with measurable ranking benefits. All improvements remain hypotheses.

**Insights.** Starting-point evidence yields three insights: (1) Electronics has 14.95% sampled wrong ranks and a −0.4812 lower-decile margin. These motivate discrimination experiments but do not establish validation performance. (2) Users report stale interests overriding current purpose. Explicit recent-history pooling could strengthen current signals, although purchases may already satisfy demand. (3) Broad associations dilute specific matches, while embedding similarity is near its neutral baseline. Severe collapse is therefore unsupported, and diversity penalties lack a diagnostic justification.

Related work supplies three insights: (1) [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) motivates multiple negatives and calibrated BCE, not evidence for candidate-set cross-entropy. (2) [HGN](https://arxiv.org/html/1906.09217) and [HAM](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10034966/) establish gated and mean-pooled recent-interest precedents. Novelty lies in the constrained adaptation, not pooling itself. (3) [R²NS](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) motivates delaying hard sampling. Uniform sampling is the simpler initial experiment.

**Framework and directions.**

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Constrained experiment |
|---|---|---|
| Candidate discrimination | gSASRec calibration | Uniform multi-negative candidate-set CE |
| Current-purpose modeling | Teddy/HGN/HAM interest separation | Gated recent-history residual |
| Behavioral succession | TGCL4SR transition graph | Training-only transition residual |

**Ideas and assessment.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder. Each cell gives a positive and negative reason.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Multi-negative gBCE | 2: principled adaptation; established | 7: reusable calibration; sampler assumptions | 4: candidate competition; no recency mechanism | 8: targets separation; margins are proxies | 3: compact loss; exclusion changes calibration |
| Gated recent residual + candidate CE | 4: targeted combination; close precedents | 7: extensible; recency can mislead | 8: targets specificity/staleness; no compatibility guarantee | 8: candidate competition; validation benefit unknown | 4: small branch; sampler/export care |
| Directed transition residual | 4: behavioral channel; established graphs | 7: sparse-history support; sparse edges | 6: succession evidence; no purpose labels | 7: collaborative discrimination; popularity shortcuts | 4: simple counts; causal integration |

**Selected idea.** Retain the recent-residual experiment, simplifying its original projection/vector gate to one scalar initialized near zero contribution. It addresses historical interests overriding current purpose and broad associations displacing specific recent matches. Candidate competition targets Electronics’ weak separation; compatibility and saturation remain unverified.

At each valid position, compute SASRec state h and masked mean m of the last five input embeddings, including the current input. Set z=h+sigmoid(a)m, a=−3. Optimize candidate-set CE against 64 unique uniform negatives excluding known training positives and the target; this objective has no sampling correction. Preserve SASRec normalization and remask padding.

Predeclare baseline, objective-only, residual-only, and combined variants, equal GPU caps, and fixed checkpoint queries. Keep routing, seeds, splits, DATA_DIR, predictor export, and diagnostic interfaces unchanged. Log every query and failure. Report paired category-stratified bootstrap intervals conditionally; they cannot remove selection bias ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Interpret pinned sampled HR@10 narrowly ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)); inspect designated users’ full-catalog recommendations separately.",
  "idea": {
    "description": "Extend each per-dataset SASRec with a causal recent-mean residual controlled by a learned scalar gate, and compare its combination with uniform multi-negative candidate-set cross-entropy against baseline and isolated-component controls. No improvement has been measured.",
    "motivation": "The recent branch explicitly targets two reported user failures: stale historical influence overriding current purpose, and broadly plausible associations crowding out specific recent interests. Candidate competition targets measured weak positive–negative separation, particularly Electronics’ 14.95% sampled wrong-rank rate, 21.15% small-margin rate, and −0.4812 lower-decile margin. Movies_and_TV is substantially stronger, while Industrial_and_Scientific and CDs_and_Vinyl are intermediate. Similar embedding-alignment scores across categories do not establish collapse as the cause. Recent interactions can also represent completed needs; neither this architecture nor histories establish compatibility, satisfaction, complementarity, or simulator traits.",
    "implementation_notes": "Preserve os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, existing input splits, and the pinned host evaluator. Honor SASREC_EPOCHS, defaulting to the supplied 200. Use the baseline optimizer, dimensions, dropout, batch construction, and other settings unchanged; record their resolved values in each checkpoint manifest. This isolates the proposed interventions and does not imply those baseline settings are optimal.

Use k=5, K=64 unique uniform negatives, and temperature tau=1 as preregistered initial settings, without tuning them in this first comparison. For position t, pool E[x_j] over nonpadding j in [max(0,t-k+1),t], dividing by max(1, valid_count). Include x_t, which is observed when predicting the next item; never include the target. Reuse the learned item embedding table, with no new embedding dropout in the residual. Compute pooling with masked cumulative sums. Let h_t be the baseline final-normalized SASRec output, and z_t=h_t+sigmoid(a)m_t with one scalar a per dataset initialized to -3. Remask padding after fusion. Add no projection or post-fusion normalization initially. The earlier projected vector gate g=sigmoid(MLP([h,r])) and LayerNorm(h+g*Wr) remain possible later extensions, but would confound information-source gains with extra capacity and normalization changes if introduced immediately.

For every valid training position, define the eligible set as real item IDs excluding the target and all items in that user's public training history. Draw min(64, eligible_count) negatives uniformly without replacement, using rejection with refill and an explicit eligible-set fallback for dense histories. If none exist, skip the position and log its count. Never inspect validation/test interactions to exclude candidates. Known-positive exclusion reduces known false negatives but can remove useful repeat-demand competition; unseen items remain uncertain. Retain IDs and exclusion sets consistently across variants. The residual-only arm uses the unchanged baseline loss and sampler; objective-only and combined arms use the new sampler. Thus the objective contrast measures the combined loss/sampler intervention, not an isolated loss effect.

Compute L=-s_pos/tau+logsumexp([s_pos/tau, s_neg_1/tau, ...]). Call this uncorrected candidate-set CE. Do not claim it estimates full-catalog softmax or that increasing negative count removes sampling bias. Mask padding positions, and defensively mask duplicate negative logits if detected; an invalid sample should normally be refilled before scoring. Do not subtract a negative-proposal log probability from the deterministically inserted positive. If a future importance-corrected objective is tested, derive probabilities for its exact user-conditioned sampler and keep it a separate experiment. gSASRec's calibration parameter t is not temperature and its evidence supports gBCE rather than this CE formulation.

Bound scoring memory by chunking valid positions. Accumulate each chunk's summed loss divided by the total valid-position count, so chunk size does not change position weights; perform one optimizer step after all chunks. Preserve gradients through shared sequence features, retaining the shared graph only as required. Log peak memory, valid-position throughput, and GPU seconds; equal epochs are not equal compute.

Predeclare four variants: baseline, objective-only, residual-only, and combined. Allocate at most 10,800 GPU seconds to each, totaling 43,200; include all four datasets, training, diagnostics, debugging, and failed runs. Within each variant use four fixed 2,700-second category envelopes, keeping categories sequential on one GPU. Use training cutoffs at 25%, 50%, and 75% of each envelope to save checkpoints, stopping training early enough to execute their three pinned validation queries and the required diagnostics within the remaining envelope. If the epoch cap is reached earlier, reuse the terminal checkpoint at later cutoffs without additional queries. If required evaluation cannot finish within the cap, record an incomplete trial rather than exceeding the budget or inventing a score. Log actual time allocations and any incomplete runs. This is a prospective budget policy, not a claim about achievable runtime.

At each checkpoint index assemble the four category checkpoints into one routed predictor, and select the index by macro validation HR@10; do not independently maximize each category's checkpoint. Compare four selected predictors, with a preregistered primary contrast of combined versus baseline and component contrasts treated as exploratory. Break exact metric ties in favor of the earlier checkpoint, then the baseline or simpler variant. Log every validation query, checkpoint, selected artifact, category result, and compute cost. Fixed seeds and limited queries reduce degrees of freedom but do not eliminate validation overfitting. Do not use the final held-out evaluation for search.

Where the pinned evaluator exposes per-user hit indicators, compute paired bootstrap differences using 10,000 resamples from an independent analysis RNG seeded 42: sample 200 users with replacement independently inside each category, use identical indices across variants, average within categories, then macro-average. Report percentile 95% intervals as conditional descriptive intervals for fixed fitted models and candidates. Apply Holm adjustment if conducting multiple confirmatory hypothesis tests; otherwise label secondary comparisons exploratory. Bootstrap intervals neither undo checkpoint/model selection nor measure training-seed, candidate-sampling, or dataset uncertainty. If per-user outcomes are unavailable, do not modify the evaluator or fabricate intervals.

Save weights, residual configuration, gate value, item mappings, resolved baseline configuration, sampler/loss settings, and selected checkpoints beneath the trial directory. Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs the complete architecture and all four routes. Use the identical pooled embeddings and fusion at inference. Verify that a saved-and-reloaded predictor reproduces in-memory scores for the same public histories and candidate IDs. Keep the scoring contract as dot products between effective features and candidate item embeddings.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). view.model must be the actual trained nn.Module; view.item_emb must expose its item table; log2feats must return effective z features; predict_score must use those same features. Preserve user_train, meta_data, and review_data compatibility without inventing unavailable fields. The loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B x L. Evaluate original positive-negative diagnostics using the supplied diagnostic negatives, rather than silently substituting training's 64-negative objective; otherwise margins become incomparable. Exclude padding and use eval mode. Return metrics and metric_definitions with explicit sampling and aggregation definitions. Empty category breakdowns are unavailable evidence, not proof of no errors; retain compatibility keys and add availability metadata if supported. The interpretation prompt must use measured values and definitions and prohibit causal or semantic conclusions unsupported by them.

For the designated twenty real training users, five per category, preserve full-catalog unseen-item recommendations. Treat qualitative feedback about current specificity, unsupported prerequisites, redundancy, and uncertainty as diagnostic evidence rather than held-out accuracy. Track these reasons only when actually reported; do not invent judgments or additional simulator calls. Available text is limited to public titles and descriptions; generic rating/review examples do not authorize ratings, reviews, prices, stores, item categories, external datasets, or pretrained weights. No new data or text channel is required for this initial experiment.

If the first comparison warrants additional research within a separately available budget, useful controls are last-item residual, fixed-weight recent mean, a parameter-matched h-only branch, normalization placement, and gate saturation/history-length analyses. These are deferred controls, not extra trials hidden inside the current four-variant budget. Watch for popularity shortcuts, embedding-norm inflation under CE, gate saturation, and gains concentrated only in dense users; interpret any such measurements as associations.",
    "pseudocode": "declare variants = [baseline, objective_only, residual_only, combined]
declare total_budget = 43200 GPU_seconds
fix preprocessing_seed = 0; training_seed = 42
fix k = 5; K = 64; tau = 1; gate_init = -3
for variant in variants:
    allocate 10800 GPU_seconds including all diagnostics and failures
    for dataset in four_categories:  # sequential, single GPU
        reset baseline training RNGs to seed 42
        load unchanged public training split and item mappings
        model = baseline_SASRec()
        if variant uses residual: add scalar parameter a = -3
        allocate fixed 2700-second category envelope
        for batch until epoch cap or preregistered training cutoff:
            h = baseline_final_normalized_features(sequence)
            if variant uses residual:
                e = item_emb(sequence) * nonpadding_mask(sequence)
                m = causal_masked_window_mean(e, sequence, k=5)
                z = (h + sigmoid(a) * m) * nonpadding_mask(sequence)
            else:
                z = h
            if variant uses candidate_CE:
                for valid positions in memory-bounded chunks:
                    A = real_items - user_training_items - {target}
                    S = uniform_without_replacement(A, min(64, len(A)))
                    if len(S) == 0: log_and_skip_position()
                    logits = dot(z, item_emb([target] + S)) / tau
                    accumulate_sum_CE_divided_by_total_valid_count(logits, target_index=0)
            else:
                compute_unchanged_baseline_loss_and_sampler(z)
            optimizer_step_once()
            save at fixed category-envelope training cutoffs: 25%, 50%, 75%
        run three pinned validation queries plus required diagnostics within envelope
        save exact architecture, mappings, configuration, timing, and weights
    for checkpoint_index in [1, 2, 3]:
        assemble four-category routed predictor at that common index
        macro_HR10[index] = mean(category_HR10_at_index)
    select common index by macro_HR10, ties favor earlier index
compare selected variants; primary contrast = combined - baseline
if per_user_hits_available:
    compute 10000 paired category-stratified bootstrap differences
log every query and actual GPU cost; do not exceed shared budget
write working/predict.py reconstructing selected complete architecture
verify checkpoint reload score parity on public histories and candidate IDs
preserve diagnosis interfaces and measured-metric interpretation prompt",
    "originality": {
      "score": 4,
      "positive": "The combination is a focused, falsifiable adaptation of recent-history fusion and candidate competition to the observed user and model failures.",
      "negative": "HGN and HAM already establish closely related gating and pooling mechanisms, and multi-negative objectives are standard; no exact-method novelty is established by the supplied searches."
    },
    "future_potential": {
      "score": 7,
      "positive": "The small residual provides an inexpensive foundation for investigating when recent evidence should modify broader sequence representations, with clear component contrasts.",
      "negative": "A scalar gate cannot explicitly distinguish satisfied purchases, compatibility constraints, or multiple purposes, and sampled HR@10 gains may not transfer to full-catalog usefulness."
    },
    "code_difficulty": {
      "score": 4,
      "positive": "The model addition requires only causal pooling and one learned scalar per dataset, reusing the baseline encoder and item embeddings.",
      "negative": "Correct user-conditioned unique sampling, memory-bounded gradients, timed comparisons, diagnostic consistency, and predictor serialization require more care than the small model change suggests."
    }
  },
  "related_work": [
    {
      "title": "Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation",
      "link": "https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1",
      "contributions": [
        "Provides the causal sequence encoder and dot-product scoring baseline.",
        "Its original implementation supplies masking and normalization conventions that should remain fixed across initial ablations."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Attention does not guarantee separation of current purpose from historical association.",
        "The original architecture contains no recent-mean fusion gate."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "gSASRec",
      "link": "https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939",
      "contributions": [
        "Studies sampled-BCE overconfidence and proposes generalized BCE.",
        "Motivates controlled experiments with more negative candidates and calibrated objectives."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Published settings are not established optima for the pinned benchmark.",
        "Its evidence supports gBCE rather than the proposed candidate-set CE.",
        "User-conditioned exclusions and deduplication change sampling assumptions relevant to calibration."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "R²NS",
      "link": "https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf",
      "contributions": [
        "Combines uniform warm-up with progressively harder stochastic negative selection."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Adds sampling complexity and possible false negatives.",
        "Reported results do not establish improvements under this evaluator."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "Teddy",
      "link": "https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ipm.2023.103619",
      "contributions": [
        "Models dominant trends and scattered interests through distinct representations."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Does not establish that a fixed recent window identifies current purpose or purchase saturation."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "TGCL4SR",
      "link": "https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28789",
      "contributions": [
        "Combines a temporal item-transition graph, time-aware Transformer, and contrastive objectives."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Observed transitions do not provide verified complementarity or compatibility labels.",
        "Its complete architecture adds complexity beyond the proposed initial experiment."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "Hierarchical Gating Networks for Sequential Recommendation",
      "link": "https://arxiv.org/html/1906.09217",
      "contributions": [
        "Applies feature and instance gates to recent item embeddings before pooling.",
        "Combines recent representations with user preferences and item-item interactions, providing a close gating precedent."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Uses SASRec as a comparator rather than as its backbone.",
        "Does not establish the proposed residual design, its gate initialization, or its performance under this benchmark."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "HAM",
      "link": "https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10034966/",
      "contributions": [
        "Provides an ungated precedent using mean pooling over shorter and longer recent windows with interaction-trained embeddings."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Does not establish novelty or effectiveness of the exact SASRec residual combination."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation",
      "link": "https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html",
      "contributions": [
        "Explains how model-selection overfitting can materially bias estimated performance."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Does not provide a benchmark-specific numerical correction for adaptive checkpoint selection."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation",
      "link": "https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/",
      "contributions": [
        "Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog rankings of algorithms."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Does not justify changing the pinned candidate evaluator or infer full-catalog gains from sampled HR@10."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "SciPy Paired Bootstrap Documentation",
      "link": "https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html",
      "contributions": [
        "Documents paired resampling principles applicable within each dataset stratum."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "The proposed macro-average stratified bootstrap requires explicit custom aggregation.",
        "Conditional bootstrap intervals do not remove adaptive model-selection bias."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "Candidate Sampling Equations",
      "link": "https://www.tensorflow.org/extras/candidate_sampling.pdf",
      "contributions": [
        "Defines sampling corrections using probabilities or expected counts matched to the candidate sampler."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Does not make uncorrected candidate-set CE a full-softmax estimator.",
        "Corrections cannot be applied indiscriminately to a deterministically inserted positive."
      ]
    }
  ]
